generation.explanation: The inscribed angle theorem says an angle with its vertex P on a circle is exactly half of the central angle ∠AOB that cuts off the same arc. So as long as P stays on the same arc, ∠APB doesn't change. Drag the yellow point P around the circle and the readout on the right stays fixed. If you move P onto the short arc between A and B, the angle becomes 180° − θ (the supplement), because P now cuts off the other arc. You can also drag A and B to change the arc, and the inscribed angle is still always half the central angle.
